rubrics.criterion: Per-quality playback data (media address, quality, dimensions, bitrate and the other attributes a playlist entry carries) is produced, distributed and consumed as one descriptor per quality throughout the pipeline: playlist parsing builds complete descriptors, and the player-core data path passes those descriptors instead of parallel member arrays.
rubrics.rationale: This case exists because the descriptor was decomposed into index-aligned columns; the regroup must reintroduce a single structure whose field list is the playlist entry, not an object that merely re-bundles the arrays.

rubrics.criterion: Current-address resolution and quality switching read the descriptor by quality (with the existing fallback to the first entry), preserving which media loads for the selected quality in the native, MP4/MSE and HLS paths, including when the synthesized auto quality is selected.
rubrics.rationale: The column form resolves addresses by array index against an implicit axis; a solver that keeps index-based resolution or only wraps the arrays has not restored the semantic grouping, and silent index drift here would select the wrong stream.

rubrics.criterion: The HLS adaptive master-playlist synthesis derives bandwidth, resolution and address from each descriptor entry, with no caller re-encoding the columns (no positional ordering dependencies and no defaulted empty columns) between the HLS component and the synthesis utility.
rubrics.rationale: The flat defaulted parameter list with an internal index zip is the deepest scatter site; the repair must make the utility's input well-defined without forcing its callers to reconstruct the grouping.

rubrics.criterion: The playlist-parsing module no longer produces member-by-member projections of the descriptor; parsing yields the complete per-quality descriptors that the rest of the pipeline consumes.
rubrics.rationale: The projection helpers are the production origin of the parallel columns; leaving them in place would mean the regrouped pipeline still depends on per-member extraction somewhere upstream, so the responsibility boundary stays split.

rubrics.criterion: The video-source distribution (context value and internal component props, including the built-in native, MP4/MSE and HLS components' prop shapes) exposes the descriptor list as one value, and no consumer of it is left reading a separately projected member axis.
rubrics.rationale: The context is the spine of the pipeline; if any built-in component still receives or forwards loose columns, the clump survives at that boundary even if parsing and the HLS utility were fixed.

rubrics.criterion: No second, separately derived per-quality collection is introduced that duplicates the descriptor list and must be kept consistent with it (for example a parallel skeleton used only as a change signal while others use the descriptor).
rubrics.rationale: The clump's cost is duplicated alignment knowledge; trading the columns for a descriptor plus a duplicate axis would reintroduce exactly that implicit-convention coupling in a new form.

rubrics.criterion: No leftover column plumbing survives in reachable code: unused parallel-array fields in prop/context types, member-projection helpers with no callers, or defaults that exist only to tolerate partially supplied columns.
rubrics.rationale: After a complete regroup, the per-column artifacts of the flattened form are dead weight that misleads the next maintainer; their persistence signals an incomplete or cosmetic repair.

rubrics.criterion: No stale alignment-contract artifacts remain in the touched modules: comments, doc notes or ordering caveats that explain how parallel values stay index-aligned after the values no longer exist in that form.
rubrics.rationale: The injected form needed documentation for its implicit axis (including where the synthetic auto entry does and does not appear); keeping that guidance after regrouping leaves misleading contracts behind.

rubrics.criterion: Quality-related event payloads and emission points are unchanged: the playback-rate/quality change events still carry their existing prev/next shape and no additional fields, and the quality lifecycle events fire at the same moments.
rubrics.rationale: The change-detection and selection paths were rewired during regrouping; these payloads are a public cross-component contract where a well-intentioned 'improvement' (e.g. attaching the new descriptor to an event) would break consumers.

rubrics.criterion: The public surface is untouched: Player still accepts the keyed playlist map and existing options without changes at call sites, the exported types and the default/named import shapes of internal modules and their barrel re-exports are preserved, and the built-in plugin selection contract behaves as before.
rubrics.rationale: This repo is consumed as a library and its plugin boundary was just opened to third parties; a repair that reshapes public props or module import surfaces to simplify the regroup would trade the clump for an integration break.
